body.working_title: Does the claimset format help LLM readers? An evaluation against the full text

body.text: When an LLM answers questions about a research paper, does giving it the paper as a claimset, instead of the full text, change how accurately it answers, and how often it states things the paper does not support?

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.1 for review: design, materials, outcomes, hypotheses and decision rules, procedure.

body.text: Hypotheses H1-H4 and their decision rules are drafted in protocol.md (AR1) but not recorded as hypothesis or plan events until the supervisor has reviewed the protocol; they will be recorded before any data are collected.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.2 for review: adds condition C4, Gemini reader models run on the supervisor's computer, and the conversion tool to be built.

body.text: Supervisor's decisions on protocol 0.1: include condition C4 (full text and claimset); reader models are Gemini models run on the supervisor's computer; the supervisor picks the papers; the study lives in a new repository claimset-org/claimset-eval. Recorded in protocol 0.2.

Converting third-party papers needs a conversion procedure that does not exist yet (claimset-submit covers a team's own work). Build a claimset-convert skill and a conversion script before the pilot; the converter is part of the treatment and is fixed after the pilot.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.3 for review: forecasting papers from arXiv PDFs, no recency requirement (memory measured by C0), question type T6 (background and positioning), readers of different capability as a design factor, alpha 0.01 with Holm across H1-H5, token and time outcomes, token budget.

body.text: Supervisor's comments on protocol 0.2: measure tokens and time; papers are arXiv PDFs in forecasting (LaTeX if available); readers of different capability (Gemini, Claude, a local open-weight model); no recency requirement; add questions on the literature review and introduction (T6); family-wise alpha 0.01 instead of 0.05. The study runs on the supervisor's computer from Claude Code. Recorded in protocol 0.3.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.3 with the converter kept in a private repository and withheld (reason commercial) in the published record.

body.text: The converter's instructions and pipeline are commercial know-how (supervisor). They are kept in a private repository; the study repository holds only their outputs, and in the published lab record they are withheld with reason commercial, keeping their hashes.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.4: open-access journal papers (by DOI) as well as arXiv; licences that permit derivatives, including non-commercial ones, with NC papers excluded from the pilot.

body.text: Supervisor's decisions on paper eligibility, before any paper was processed: papers may be open-access journal articles identified by DOI as well as arXiv versions; any Creative Commons licence that permits derivatives is eligible, including CC BY-NC and CC BY-NC-SA (claimset specification v0.13, rule 31), because the study is open, non-commercial research on the format, not an evaluation of the converter. Derived documents keep the paper's licence conditions, and NC papers are kept away from commercial work: since the pilot develops the commercial converter, pilot papers must not be NC. Recorded in protocol 0.4.

Supervisor's decisions on paper eligibility, before any paper was processed: papers may be open-access journal articles identified by DOI as well as arXiv versions; any Creative Commons licence that permits derivatives is eligible, including CC BY-NC and CC BY-NC-SA (claimset specification v0.13, rule 31), because the study is open, non-commercial research on the format, not an evaluation of the converter; derived documents keep the paper's licence conditions, and NC papers are kept away from commercial work. Proposed by AC2 as a consequence, awaiting the supervisor's confirmation: since the pilot develops the commercial converter, pilot papers must not be NC. Recorded in protocol 0.4.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.5: NC papers are eligible for the pilot as well as the confirmatory set; nothing from an NC paper is copied into the private converter repository.

body.text: Supervisor's decision on AC2's proposal in DC7: the proposal is rejected. NC papers are eligible for the pilot, because this is research; the pilot includes Staying positive (CC BY-NC 4.0). Nothing from an NC paper (text, excerpts, claimset, fidelity report or examples) is ever copied into the private converter repository, its instructions, tests or examples. Recorded in protocol 0.5.

AC4 is a duplicate registration of the same agent as AC3 (Claude Code (local), claude-opus-5-5), made by mistake after the supervisor had already registered AC3. AC4 is not used; this agent writes as AC3.
